sheet-1.description: The western end of Margate City at the Longport line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch as sheet 132 of the Atlantic City volume. The sheet runs from the Borough of Longport boundary, a dash-dot line just west of Jackson Avenue, east to Washington Avenue, and from Winchester Avenue (Arctic Avenue) south across Ventnor Avenue (Atlantic Avenue), Pacific Avenue (Longport Speedway) and Atlantic Avenue to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean. The cross streets are Jackson, Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams and Washington Avenues. Atlantic Avenue carries the double track of the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, electric and steam). The blocks are platted into narrow lots and are thinly built: scattered frame dwellings, private garages and sheds, with most building in the blocks between Jefferson and Washington Avenues. Named buildings are Trinity M.E. Church with its chapel on Ventnor Avenue at Madison, a hotel and bath house by the beach at Jefferson Avenue, the Hickey Club with its bath house on Atlantic Avenue at Washington, and a pavilion and Lennig store on the Longport line at Atlantic Avenue. Inclines lead up to the Boardwalk at Jackson and Jefferson Avenues, and one dwelling south of Atlantic Avenue stands on piles. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. The south part of the sheet is open ocean; the blank blocks north of Winchester Avenue belong to sheet 137.
notes: Jackson Avenue is now Coolidge Avenue (North and South Coolidge Avenue).
Ventnor Avenue is labelled with its former name Atlantic Avenue, Winchester Avenue as Arctic Avenue and Pacific Avenue as Longport Speedway.
Trinity M.E. Church and chapel, Ventnor Avenue at Madison Avenue.
Hickey Club and bath house, Atlantic Avenue at Washington Avenue.

Atlantic City vol. sheet 132, 100 ft. One part: Jackson (now Coolidge), Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams, Washington Av between Winchester (Arctic), Ventnor (Atlantic), Pacific (Longport Speedway), Atlantic Av and the Boardwalk; Longport/Margate boundary at left; Trinity M.E. Church, Hickey Club.

sheet-2.description: Central Margate City at 100 ft to an inch, sheet 133 of the Atlantic City volume, from Washington Avenue east to Sumner Avenue and from Winchester Avenue (Arctic) south to the Boardwalk. The cross streets are Washington, Decatur, Benson, Cedar Grove (80 ft), Vendome, Union, Thurlow and Sumner Avenues; Ventnor Avenue widens east of Cedar Grove Avenue into Ventnor Parkway, 180 ft wide, and Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore and West Jersey and Seashore railroad tracks. Pacific Avenue appears only at the west edge. The northern blocks are platted into numbered lots with almost no buildings. The civic centre is at Washington and Ventnor Avenues: City Hall with the fire department (one chief, two paid men, 43 volunteers, a triple combination engine and hose) and a hotel on Atlantic Avenue. On Atlantic Avenue at Benson Avenue stand the Sea View Hotel and stores. South of Atlantic Avenue lie the Elephant Hotel with its cafe and The Elephant, the elephant-shaped building, with a bath house. The beach blocks west of Cedar Grove Avenue are cut short by water, and the shore east of it is protected by a line of bulkhead reaching the Boardwalk, which is drawn along the sheet with an incline at Cedar Grove Avenue. Below that is open Atlantic Ocean.
notes: Ventnor Parkway (180 ft) is now Ventnor Avenue with its North and South Ventnor Avenue service roads.
Cedar Grove Avenue north of Ventnor Avenue is now North Harding Avenue; south of it the name survives.
City Hall and fire department, Washington Avenue at Ventnor Avenue.
Elephant Hotel and The Elephant (the elephant-shaped building) south of Atlantic Avenue near Benson Avenue.
Sea View Hotel, Atlantic Avenue at Benson Avenue.

Sheet 133, 100 ft. One part: Washington, Decatur, Benson, Cedar Grove, Vendome, Union, Thurlow, Sumner Av between Winchester, Ventnor Av / Ventnor Parkway (180 ft), Atlantic Av and the Boardwalk; City Hall and fire dept, Sea View Hotel, Elephant Hotel and The Elephant (Lucy). Lower left below Atlantic is beach without blocks.

sheet-3.description: Margate City from Sumner Avenue east to Mansfield Avenue, sheet 134 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch. The part runs from Winchester Avenue south across Ventnor Parkway, drawn 180 ft wide with its water main, and Atlantic Avenue, which carries the Atlantic City and Shore and West Jersey and Seashore railroad tracks, to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean. The cross streets are Sumner, Rumson, Quincy, Pembroke, Osborne, Nassau and Mansfield Avenues. Every block is platted into numbered lots, but the district is almost empty: a few dwellings with garages on Winchester and Quincy Avenues, a concrete dwelling on Osborne Avenue, an office on Atlantic Avenue at Mansfield, and a handful of dwellings on the beach blocks near Nassau Avenue, one of them partly built. The beach blocks end at a line of bulkhead with the Boardwalk outside it, and the beach block east of Nassau Avenue narrows towards the shore. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the avenues. The sheet edges show the adjoining sheets 133, 135 and 139, and the southern half of the sheet is open ocean.
notes: Ventnor Parkway is now Ventnor Avenue with North and South Ventnor Avenue service roads; its junctions were not detected (wide unbuilt parkway).
Sheet 134, 100 ft. One part: Sumner, Rumson, Quincy, Pembroke, Osborne, Nassau, Mansfield Av between Winchester, Ventnor Parkway, Atlantic Av and the Boardwalk. Almost no buildings.

sheet-4.description: Eastern Margate City between Mansfield and Frontenac Avenues, sheet 135 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch. The street pattern is irregular: Winchester Avenue (partly not open) crosses the top of the sheet, and below it Ventnor Avenue and Winchester Road run diagonally, meeting near Iroquois Avenue, before Atlantic Avenue with the Atlantic City and Shore and West Jersey and Seashore railroad tracks runs straight across the sheet. North of Ventnor Avenue the cross streets are Cairo, Davenport, Iroquois and Huntington Avenues, with Gladstone Avenue at the east; south of Winchester Road they are Kenyon, Jerome, Jasper, Iroquois, Huntington, Granville, Gladstone and Frontenac Avenues, and Mansfield and Lancaster Avenues at the west edge. Most blocks are large and undivided (blocks 109 to 113, 209, 211), others platted into lots; there are almost no buildings, only a store and dwelling on Atlantic Avenue at Gladstone Avenue and two buildings near Mansfield Avenue. South of Atlantic Avenue are beach blocks 7 to 13, with the high-water line crossing them, a bulkhead on Atlantic Avenue at the east, and the Boardwalk only at the west end. Ventnor Parkway enters at the west edge.
notes: Ventnor Avenue and Winchester Road are drawn diagonally across the sheet; modern Ventnor Avenue runs straight, and modern Knight, Hanover and Haverford Avenues cut through the large 1921 blocks.
Cairo and Davenport Avenues north of Ventnor Avenue do not match modern streets directly and were not used as control.
Winchester Avenue west of Cairo Avenue is marked not open.

Sheet 135, 100 ft. One part: Mansfield to Frontenac Av; Winchester Av (not open), Ventnor Av and Winchester Rd running diagonally, Atlantic Av; Cairo and Davenport Av north of Ventnor, Kenyon, Jerome, Jasper, Iroquois, Huntington, Granville, Gladstone Av; beach blocks 7 to 13 south of Atlantic.

sheet-5.description: The eastern end of Margate City at the Ventnor City line, sheet 136 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch. The part runs from Frontenac Avenue east to Fredericksburg Avenue, which marks the Margate City and City of Ventnor boundary, and from Winchester Avenue and Winchester Road south across Ventnor Avenue and Atlantic Avenue to the Boardwalk. North of Atlantic Avenue the cross streets are Frontenac, Franklin Square, Essex, Douglas, Clermont, Brunswick and Argyle Avenues (Argyle 50 ft 4 in wide), with Franklin and Essex Avenues north of Ventnor; south of it are Exeter, Douglas, Delaware, Clermont, Clarendon, Brunswick, Barclay and Andover Avenues. Ogontz and Wilmington Avenues appear at the top edge. The blocks are mostly large and empty, lettered A to D north of Winchester Road. A branch of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad trolley line leaves Atlantic Avenue diagonally across block 104, and the Savannah Avenue trolley station stands on Atlantic Avenue at Douglas Avenue. Buildings are few: dwellings and garages at Frontenac and Franklin, the Bell Telephone Company exchange near Essex Avenue, and a store by the trolley line. The beach blocks end at a bulkhead with the Boardwalk outside it.
notes: Delaware Avenue is now South Delavan Avenue.
Clermont is printed Clearmont Avenue.
Exeter and Essex Avenue junctions with Atlantic Avenue were 11 to 12 m off the fit and were rejected; these streets do not lie on their 1921 lines.
Savannah Avenue trolley station and the diverging West Jersey and Seashore trolley line on block 104.
Bell Telephone Company exchange near Essex Avenue.

Sheet 136, 100 ft. One part: Frontenac to Fredericksburg Av (Margate/Ventnor line): Franklin, Essex, Douglas, Clermont, Brunswick, Argyle, Delaware, Clarendon, Barclay, Andover Av between Winchester Av, Winchester Rd, Ventnor, Atlantic Av and the Boardwalk; trolley line of the W.J.&S.R.R. curving off Atlantic Av.

sheet-6.description: The bay side of western Margate City, sheet 137 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch, from the Borough of Longport line at Jackson Avenue east to Washington Avenue. The part runs from Winchester Avenue (Arctic) north across Monmouth Avenue (Baltic) to Thoroughfare Avenue (Amherst Avenue) on the shore of Beach Thoroughfare, whose open water and far shore fill the upper half of the sheet. The cross streets are Jackson, Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams and Washington Avenues; Massey Avenue and Bayview Avenue are short streets in the blocks between Jefferson and Washington. A tidal creek winds from the thoroughfare across block 429 between Madison and Jefferson Avenues and the shoreline crosses the north ends of the blocks. Building is scattered: frame dwellings and garages, densest near Jackson Avenue on the Longport line and along Bayview Avenue, where a row of twelve small cottages stands, with a club house nearby. Billy's Hotel stands on Thoroughfare Avenue at Washington Avenue, with a comfort station by Adams Avenue and a sewer blow-off at the thoroughfare. Water mains run in Monmouth and Winchester Avenues. The blocks south of Winchester Avenue belong to sheet 132.
notes: Thoroughfare Avenue is now Amherst Avenue; Jackson Avenue is now Coolidge Avenue.
Massey Avenue and Bayview Avenue are not in the modern street data.
Billy's Hotel, Thoroughfare Avenue at Washington Avenue.

Sheet 137, 100 ft. One part: bay side, Jackson (Coolidge) to Washington Av between Winchester (Arctic), Monmouth (Baltic), Massey Av and Thoroughfare (Amherst) Av; Beach Thoroughfare, creek through block 429; upper half blank water.

sheet-7.description: The bay side of central Margate City, sheet 138 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch. The part runs from Washington Avenue east to Sumner Avenue between Winchester Avenue (Arctic) and Thoroughfare Avenue (Amherst Avenue), and north of Amherst Avenue between Union and Thurlow Avenues up across Fremont and Fulton Avenues to Wellington Avenue. The cross streets are Washington, Decatur, Benson, Cedar Grove, Vendome, Union, Thurlow and Sumner Avenues, with Monmouth Avenue (Baltic) between Winchester and Amherst. Beach Thoroughfare fills the northwest of the sheet, its shore running diagonally past a line of dwellings on lots facing the water; a tidal creek (high water line) loops through blocks 424 and 524 between Benson and Cedar Grove Avenues, and Sunset Canal runs along the east side of the Thurlow Avenue lots. The blocks are platted into numbered lots and mostly empty. The Margate City Water Works pumping station with its pumps, steel reservoir and repair shop stands on Decatur Avenue, and the public school, heated by hot air and lit by electricity, on Winchester Avenue between Vendome and Union Avenues. A restaurant and dwellings stand at Washington and Thoroughfare Avenues, with a sewer blow-off at the shore.
notes: Cedar Grove Avenue here is now North Harding Avenue.
Margate City Water Works pumping station, Decatur Avenue.
Public school on Winchester Avenue between Vendome and Union Avenues.
Winchester Avenue at the bottom edge was left out as control: only its north edge is drawn and the detector paired it with a lot line about 50 ft inside the block.

Sheet 138, 100 ft. One part: bay side, Washington to Sumner Av between Winchester, Monmouth (Baltic), Thoroughfare/Amherst Av, Fremont, Fulton and Wellington Av; Margate City Water Works pumping station, public school; Beach Thoroughfare and Sunset Canal.

sheet-8.description: The bay side of Margate City from Sumner Avenue east to Mansfield Avenue and Cario Avenue, sheet 139 of the Atlantic City volume at 100 ft to an inch. The part runs from Winchester Avenue north across Monmouth and Amherst Avenues to Freemont and Fulton Avenues on Beach Thoroughfare. The cross streets are Sumner, Rumson, Quincy, Pembroke, Osborne, Nassau and Mansfield Avenues, with Cario Avenue at the east edge. North of Amherst Avenue the land is cut by dredged waterways: Sunset Canal on the west, Orient Canal between Pembroke and Nassau Avenues, and The Raceway, which joins them along the south side of the blocks between Rumson and Pembroke Avenues, so that those blocks with Fulton and Freemont Avenues form an island bounded by water on three sides. All blocks are platted into numbered lots; buildings are only a few dwellings and garages in the blocks between Monmouth and Winchester Avenues, chiefly near Sumner, Rumson and Nassau Avenues. The open water of Beach Thoroughfare fills the top of the sheet, with its shore curving up to the northeast corner. Water pipes run in Winchester and Monmouth Avenues, and the adjoining sheets 134, 135 and 138 are marked at the edges.
notes: Freemont Avenue is now Fremont Avenue.
Cario Avenue at the east edge (probably the Cairo Avenue of sheet 135) was not matched to a modern street.
Winchester Avenue at the bottom edge was left out as control (only one edge drawn).
Sunset Canal, Orient Canal and The Raceway enclose the Rumson to Pembroke Avenue blocks north of Amherst Avenue.

Sheet 139, 100 ft. One part: bay side, Sumner to Mansfield Av and Cairo Av between Winchester, Monmouth, Amherst, Freemont and Fulton Av; Sunset Canal, Orient Canal and The Raceway enclosing the Rumson/Pembroke blocks.
